Build visually stunning, fully functional web UIs. ALWAYS apply these rules when building any HTML/CSS/JS app:

1. DESIGN: Use a dark background (e.g. background: linear-gradient(135deg, #0f0c29, #302b63, #24243e)). Import Google Fonts (Outfit, Inter, or Poppins). Use glassmorphism cards (background: rgba(255,255,255,0.05); backdrop-filter: blur(20px); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1); border-radius: 16px).

2. COLORS: Never use plain red/blue/green. Use curated palettes: X player = #a78bfa (purple), O player = #f472b6 (pink), success = #34d399 (green), text = rgba(255,255,255,0.85).

3. ANIMATIONS: Add CSS keyframe animations. Use 'popIn' for elements appearing (transform: scale(0) to scale(1) with cubic-bezier(0.175, 0.885, 0.32, 1.275)). Add hover:transform:scale(1.03) and hover:box-shadow on interactive elements. Add transition: all 0.2s ease to all interactive elements.

4. LAYOUT: Center everything with flexbox (display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; min-height:100vh). Use CSS Grid for game boards. Cells must be at LEAST 130px x 130px. Font sizes for game symbols must be at LEAST 3rem.

5. GAME UI PATTERN: Always include: (a) a status banner showing whose turn it is, (b) a scoreboard tracking wins/draws across rounds, (c) a win overlay/modal with animation when someone wins, (d) a 'New Round' button and a 'Reset All' button.

6. INTERACTIVITY: All clickable elements must have :hover and :active states. Use user-select:none on game cells. Add ripple or pulse effects on click.

7. SELF-CONTAINED: Write everything in a SINGLE index.html file with <style> and <script> inline. Do NOT split into separate CSS/JS files unless the user explicitly asks.

8. VERIFICATION: After writing the file, ALWAYS run: start "" "FULL_PATH_TO_INDEX.HTML" to open it in the browser so the user can see it immediately. Wrap the path in double quotes to handle spaces in folder names.

9. WHOLE FILE REWRITES: When the user asks to improve, redesign, fix errors, or add features to an existing file — ALWAYS use readFile to read the current content first, then use writeFile to write the COMPLETE new file from top to bottom. NEVER use replaceFileContent for redesigns or large changes — it will break the file if the target text doesn't match exactly. Only use replaceFileContent for tiny 1-2 line surgical fixes where you are 100% certain the target text exists verbatim.

Build 2-player browser games (tic-tac-toe, chess, checkers, etc). Always use the $premium-ui skill patterns. Game logic rules: use a flat array for board state, define WINNING_COMBOS as a constant array, use currentPlayer toggling between two values, implement checkWinner() that returns winner object with {player, combo}, highlight winning cells with a 'winning' CSS class, show a win/draw modal overlay after 700ms delay so animations complete first. Always include score tracking that persists across rounds.

CRITICAL RULE FOR EDITING EXISTING FILES:

DECISION TREE — always follow this before editing any file:

Q: Is the user asking to redesign, improve, add animations, fix bugs, or make the UI better?
A: YES → Use readFile to read the FULL current file → Then use writeFile to write the COMPLETE new version from scratch. Include ALL existing functionality PLUS the new improvements. Never leave anything out.

Q: Is the user asking to fix a tiny specific thing (e.g. change one color, fix one typo, update one variable)?
A: YES → Only then use replaceFileContent. But first use readFile to verify the EXACT target text exists verbatim before attempting the replacement.

WHY THIS MATTERS: replaceFileContent searches for an exact string match. If the target text has even one character difference (extra space, different quote style, etc), the replacement FAILS and the file becomes blank or broken. For any change larger than 2 lines, always use writeFile with the complete file content instead.

AFTER ANY EDIT: Always run start "" "FULL_FILE_PATH" to verify the result opens correctly in the browser.
